summary: On 11 March 2011, a strong earthquake happened under the sea near Japan. Part of the sea floor moved. This helped cause a tsunami, a set of large waves. The waves reached the coast of the Tohoku region. This lesson looks at some effects and the work to recover. People and places were not all affected in the same way.

cards.title: Homes and shelter
cards.text: Some homes were damaged. People used shared shelters in the first days.
cards.time: Short term; longer effects may be justified
cards.reason: Homes are places. People needed somewhere to stay. The card names the first days.

cards.title: Roads and travel
cards.text: Some roads and rail lines were damaged. This made travel hard at first.
cards.time: Short term; long term if repair evidence is linked
cards.reason: Roads and rail lines are places and routes. People found travel hard. The card says at first.

cards.title: Water and power
cards.text: At first, power and water supplies stopped in some areas.
cards.time: Short term focus; no exact outage length claimed
cards.reason: The card says at first. Services stopped, affecting places and the people who use them. The length of each outage is not stated.

cards.title: Rebuilding
cards.text: Homes and transport routes were rebuilt over months and years.
cards.reason: Built places changed. People used them. The card names months and years.

cards.title: Homes for a time
cards.text: Some people used temporary homes. Work to build new homes went on for years.
cards.reason: The card names housing work over years. Temporary does not always mean only a few days.

cards.title: Sea walls
cards.text: Some places on the coast rebuilt sea walls over years.
cards.focus: Places and people with an explained link
cards.reason: These are changes to coastal places. They were intended to reduce future harm to people and places; they do not remove all risk.

image_text.Effect_Model.png:
One effect can fit both
E1: Some homes were damaged. People used shared shelters in the first days.
People: a place to stay.
Places: homes and shelters.
Time: short term. The card names the first days.
A longer effect needs a fact about a longer time.
image_text.Sort_Guide.png:
Two separate checks for each card
Focus: people / places / both.
Time: short term / long term / both.
Short term: first hours and days in this task.
Long term: months and years in this task.
Choose a focus. Then choose a time. Use a fact to say why.
Both is allowed if the reason fits.

model: I read E1. It says homes were damaged and people used shelters. I choose both people and places. I choose short term because it says the first days. Homes can take longer to rebuild, but I need another fact to show that.
